title: Documentation
concept: `xiom doc` generates HTML documentation from doc comments in source code
why: Code without documentation is a puzzle. `xiom doc` automates documentation generation so your API docs stay in sync with your code. Doc comments live right next to the implementation, making it easy to update docs when you change behavior. Generated docs are the first thing users see — they determine whether someone adopts your library.
theory: `xiom doc` parses all `.xi` files in a project, extracts `///` and `//!` doc comments, and renders them as static HTML. It generates pages for every public item: modules, functions, structs, enums, traits, and type aliases. The output includes a search index, cross-references between types, and syntax-highlighted code. Documentation can be built for local viewing (`xiom doc --open`) or published to the XIOM package registry alongside the crate.
syntax_ref:
xiom doc                    # generate docs
xiom doc --open             # generate and open in browser
xiom doc --no-deps          # skip dependency docs
tips: Write doc comments for every `pub` item — users depend on them
Use `//!` for module-level docs, `///` for item-level docs
Run `xiom doc` and review the output before publishing a crate
common_mistakes: Writing doc comments for private items (they won't appear in output)
Forgetting to include code examples in doc comments
Using `//` instead of `///` — plain comments are ignored by xiom doc
